title: After eating, we went to the pagoda
title_target: ထမင်း စားပြီးတော့ ဘုရား သွားတယ် — hta-miⁿ: sa:-pyee:-dò. hpa.ya: thwa:-dè
goal: Joining several events into one flowing story — using linking words that, like every Burmese marker, stand after the part they link.
bekal: joining two events with ပြီးတော့
expressing contrast with ဒါပေမဲ့
giving a reason with …လို့ and ဒါကြောင့်
telling about a whole day without stopping at every sentence

dialogs.title: စကားပြော — Telling about Sunday
dialogs.intro: Ko Zaw asks Ani about her Sunday. Notice that Ani's answers are no longer short sentences standing alone: she links them with ပြီးတော့, ဒါပေမဲ့, and …လို့ until the story flows.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [တနင်္ဂနွေနေ့|ta.niⁿ-ga.nway-nay.] [ဘာ|ba] [လုပ်|lohk] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: What did you do on Sunday?

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [မနက်|ma.nèk] [စောစော|sò-sò] [ထ|hta.] [ပြီးတော့|pyee:-dò.] [ဈေး|zay:] [သွား|thwa:] [တယ်|dè]။
lines.id: I got up early and went to the market.
lines.literal: morning — early-early — get-up — then — market — go — statement.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [သစ်သီး|thik-thee:] [နဲ့|nè.] [ငါး|nga:] [ဝယ်|wè] [တယ်|dè]။ [ပြီးတော့|pyee:-dò.] [အိမ်|ayⁿ] [ပြန်|pyaⁿ] [ပြီး|pyee:] [ချက်|hchèk] [တယ်|dè]။
lines.id: Fruit and fish. Then I went home and cooked.
lines.literal: fruit — and — fish — buy — statement. then — home — return — then — cook — statement.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ငါး|nga:] [ဟင်း|hiⁿ:] [ချက်|hchèk] [တယ်|dè]။ [ဒါပေမဲ့|da-bay-mè.] [သိပ်|thayk] [မ|ma.] [ကောင်း|kowⁿ:] [ဘူး|boo:]။
lines.id: Fish curry. But it wasn't very good.
lines.literal: fish — curry — cook — statement. but — too — not — be-good — not.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ဘာဖြစ်လို့|ba-hpyik-loh.] [လဲ|lè:]။

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ငါးပိ|nga.pee.] [မ|ma.] [ထည့်|htè.] [တတ်|tak] [လို့|loh.] [ပါ|ba]။ [နောက်တစ်ခါ|nowk-ta.hka] [မြမြ|mya.mya.] [ကို|koh] [မေး|may:] [မယ်|mè]။
lines.id: Because I don't know how to use fish paste yet. Next time I'll ask Mya Mya.
lines.literal: fish-paste — not — put-in — know-how — because — polite. next-time — mya-mya — object — ask — will.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ညနေ|nya.-nay] [ရွှေတိဂုံ|shway-da.gohⁿ] [သွား|thwa:] [တယ်|dè]။ [လူ|loo] [အရမ်း|a.yaⁿ:] [များ|mya:] [လို့|loh.] [ခဏ|hka.na.] [ပဲ|bè:] [နေ|nay] [တယ်|dè]။
lines.id: In the afternoon I went to Shwedagon. It was so crowded I only stayed a little while.
lines.literal: afternoon — shwedagon — go — statement. people — very — be-many — because — a-moment — only — stay — statement.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [တနင်္ဂနွေနေ့|ta.niⁿ-ga.nway-nay.] [ဆိုတော့|hsoh-dò.] [အမြဲ|a.myè:] [လူများ|loo-mya:] [တယ်|dè]။ [စနေနေ့|sa.nay-nay.] [မနက်|ma.nèk] [က|ga.] [ပို|poh] [ငြိမ်|ngyayⁿ] [တယ်|dè]။
lines.id: It's Sunday, so it's always crowded. Saturday morning is quieter.
lines.literal: sunday-day — because — always — people-many — statement. saturday-day — morning — the — more — be-quiet — statement.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဟုတ်လား|hohk-la:]။ [ဒါဆို|da-hsoh] [နောက်တစ်ခါ|nowk-ta.hka] [စနေနေ့|sa.nay-nay.] [သွား|thwa:] [မယ်|mè]။
lines.id: Really? Then next time I'll go on Saturday.
lines.literal: true-Q. in-that-case — next-time — saturday-day — go — will.

grammars.title: ပြီးတော့ and ပြီး — and then, after that
body: To join two events in sequence, the first verb ends in **ပြီး** and the sentence carries on. The long form, **ပြီးတော့**, is a bit more emphatic and often stands at the start of a new sentence.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: ထပြီး ရေချိုးတယ်
အိမ် ပြန်ပြီး ချက်တယ်

after: ⚠️ Remember the difference from unit 11: **ပြီး** (*pyee:*, high tone) means "done, and then"; **ပြီ** (*bee*, level tone) means "already". Swapping them changes the meaning of the sentence completely.

You can chain more than two events: ထပြီး ရေချိုးပြီး မနက်စာ စားပြီးတော့ ရုံး သွားတယ် — "got up, showered, had breakfast, then went to the office". This is how people in Myanmar tell about their day in a single breath.

grammars.title: ဒါပေမဲ့ — but
body: Contrast is expressed with ဒါပေမဲ့ (*da-bay-mè.*), which stands **at the start** of the second sentence — the one important linking word that isn't placed at the back.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: another spelling of ဒါပေမဲ့

after: The short form, **…ပေမဲ့**, attaches straight to the verb and means "although": ဈေးကြီးပေမဲ့ ဝယ်တယ် (it was expensive, but I bought it anyway). It's more compact and very common.

grammars.title: …လို့ — because
body: A reason is expressed with လို့ (*loh.*) attached to the verb of the cause, and the reason clause comes **first** — the opposite of English, which usually puts "because" second.

head: Burmese
Say it
Literal translation
Meaning
rows: လူများလို့ ခဏပဲ နေတယ်
it was crowded, so I didn't stay long
မအားလို့ မလာဘူး
didn't come because I was busy
didn't go because of the rain
မထည့်တတ်လို့ပါ
because I don't know how to use it yet

after: ⚠️ To answer the question **ဘာဖြစ်လို့လဲ** ("why?"), the reason alone ending in **လို့ပါ** is enough: မအားလို့ပါ ("because I was busy"). It's a full, polite answer; no need to repeat the whole sentence.
လို့ also appears in …လို့ ရလား (unit 12) and …လို့ ခေါ်တယ် (unit 4). One small word with several jobs, and its place in the sentence decides the meaning.

grammars.title: …ဆိုတော့ — since, given that
body: ဆိုတော့ (*hsoh-dò.*) gives a reason that is **a situation or a fact**, not an action. You've seen it since unit 4.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: တနင်္ဂနွေနေ့ ဆိုတော့

after: In short: **လို့ for a reason that's an action or a state with a verb**, **ဆိုတော့ for a reason that's a thing, a person, or a fact**. When in doubt, လို့ is right more often.

blocks.text: Up to unit 17, your sentences stood on their own. From now on you can link them. Here's a whole day, strung together with the linking words you've just learned — read it aloud in one breath.

head: Burmese
Say it
rows: မနက် စောစော ထပြီး ရေချိုးတယ်။
ရုံးမှာ အလုပ် များလို့ နေ့လယ်စာ မစားရဘူး။
ညနေ အိမ် ပြန်ပြီး ညစာ ချက်တယ်။
ပင်ပန်းပေမဲ့ ပျော်တယ်။

blocks.text: Those five sentences hold nine verbs, three linking words, one reason, and one contrast — and **not one verb changes form**. If you can build a paragraph like this about your own day, you've got A1 Burmese in hand.

blocks.title: Linking words you need
items: **ပြီးတော့** — and then, after that. The most common one; if you can learn only one, learn this.
**ဒါပေမဲ့** — but. Stands at the start of the second sentence.
**…လို့** — because. The reason comes first, the result follows.
**ဒါကြောင့်** — so, therefore. The reverse order of …လို့: the reason has been stated, and this links on the result.
**…ရင်** — if (unit 7). **…ပေမဲ့** — although. Both attach to the verb.

တယ် / နေ / ခဏပဲ / လူများလို့
What did you do on Sunday?

Then I went home and cooked.
But it wasn't very good.
Why?
It was crowded, so I only stayed a little while.
